messages:
Priya Nair: noticing a sustained spike of connection resets and 5xxs on the inference edge since 02:03 UTC, WAF is firing a bunch of rules. seeing a lot of short-lived TCP conn resets from multiple /20 ranges. anyone oncall?
Alex Chen: oncall here. can you paste the WAF alert IDs and any example ips?
Priya Nair: alert ids: waf-7321, waf-7322. sample ips: 34.124.0.0/20, 13.89.64.0/20, 3.12.96.0/20. counts: ~18k req/min to /v1/generate chat endpoints, errors spiking to 12%.
Maya Ortiz: tagging security. quick question: do we have any evidence of credential scraping or KMS key usage anomalies? if not, treat as traffic abuse.
Jonah Park: ok i'll push a temporary connection rate limit and add an ipset for those prefixes. planning to add a WAF rule to block if rate>200rps per src over 1m window.
Alex Chen: add canary to 10% of edge first, then roll if good. include automatic rollback after 5m if backend errors increase.
Jonah Park: applying ipset now:
```bash
# create ipset
ipset create ddos-probe hash:net -exist
ipset add ddos-probe 34.124.0.0/20
ipset add ddos-probe 13.89.64.0/20
ipset add ddos-probe 3.12.96.0/20
# attach to waf rule (pseudo)
apply-waf-rule --name block-ddos-probe --match src_ipset=ddos-probe --action block --scope canary
```
deploy-bot: waf rule block-ddos-probe deployed to canary (10%) at 02:11 UTC, rule-id wfr-8812.
Priya Nair: after canary, error rate dropped to 4% and request volume down 70% for those prefixes. customers are seeing fewer failures.
Evan (Customer Success): which customers were affected? we need a list to proactively notify if they saw 503s.
Alex Chen: compiling list, looks like customer ids: C-241, C-998, C-177. Affected routes were /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings ingest from those src blocks.
Maya Ortiz: we should lock down RBAC on WAF edits while this is active. only infra-sre and security should be able to change rules. I'll open a short-lived policy that restricts the waf:UpdateRule action and ensure changes are audit-logged to the central bucket encrypted with KMS.
Priya Nair: can you add an audit checkpoint and export current ACLs? want to capture pre-change state.
Maya Ortiz: doing that now. audit-checkpoint id: ac-20240324-02. Also enabling higher-fidelity request logging for the canary so we can look for payload patterns for vuln triage.
Jonah Park: rolling the rule to 100% now and enabling a softer rate-limit first then block if behavior persists. Config snippet:
```json
{
  "rule": "rate-limit-src-1m",
  "threshold": 200,
  "window": 60,
  "action": "challenge_then_block",
  "fallback": "503_when_overloaded"
}
```
deploy-bot: rule wfr-8812 rolled to 100% at 02:23 UTC.
Priya Nair: traffic from those prefixes now down 88%, global 5xxs back to baseline. good containment.
Maya Ortiz: security note: request logs show high-frequency probes hitting /v1/metadata and /v1/health as well — looks like horizontal scanning. no suspicious KMS key usage seen in the last 24h.
security-bot: alert cloud-provider: detected suspicious scanner VM churn associated with 3 suspicious accounts, flagged for abuse.
Maya Ortiz: for remediation: 1) increase audit log retention for WAF and KMS logs to 90d for now 2) rotate any service creds used by edge ingestion (we'll check secrets-manager access logs) 3) create RBAC policy that requires two-person approval for production WAF edits for 24h window.
Alex Chen: done: created temporary policy role: role/waf-emergency-edit with approval required. Added to the infra-sre and security groups.
Jonah Park: confirmed no elevated KMS decrypt counts, here's a snippet from the audit log (sanitized):
```
2024-03-24T02:10:21Z audit: service=edge component=proxy event=conn_reset src=34.124.3.21 dst=api-1 prod_route=/v1/generate
2024-03-24T02:12:05Z audit: waf event=rule_triggered rule=wfr-8812 src=13.89.66.77 action=challenge
```
Priya Nair: customer impact comms: I drafted a short note for C-241/C-998/C-177 explaining transient availability and mitigations, will send once legal signs off.
Evan (Customer Success): thanks, pls cc infra and security in the note. we'll offer a short SLA credit if they had measurable errors.
Maya Ortiz: next steps / post-incident actions: - formal postmortem with timeline - add WAF edit runbook and RBAC play for emergency changes - tune rate-limit thresholds per route (not global) - schedule a follow-up with cloud provider to request permanent block of offending accounts/IPs - enable KMS key access anomaly alerts
Alex Chen: i'll own the runbook and the per-route tuning, target EOD tomorrow.
Jonah Park: i'll add an automated ipset update job that pulls from cloud-provider-abuse feed and puts items into a review queue.
Priya Nair: thanks all — closing the active incident channel in 30m, leaving postmortem notes in #postmortems later today. :white_check_mark:
Maya Ortiz: adding a reminder to rotate any short-lived credentials issued during the incident. also scheduling a 1-hour incident review at 16:00 UTC. :calendar:
Alex Chen: small follow-up: deploy-bot reported one brief rollback during canary but rollback was automatic and healthy. logging it in the postmortem.
deploy-bot: rollback event recorded for wfr-8812 at 02:15 UTC, reason: transient backend error > rollback-threshold.
Priya Nair: great job team. happy to close after postmortem action items are assigned. :thumbsup:
